findings.text: The first paragraph says what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A newcomer can say what it is and why it matters before scrolling.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The header links straight to concrete next steps: prerequisites, a clone command, ./setup.sh, and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"`. What to do next is clear and easy to reach.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" (header) and the Next steps section

findings.text: Someone visiting Athena's site meets a title about a different project, firstmate. Almost all of the page is firstmate's internals, so a newcomer may wonder whether they are on the right page until they read the second paragraph.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>; h1 "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The page promises that every commit can be traced to its request, models, cost and verdict, but never shows an example. The study proves that claims are traced to sources, not that runs are costed and checked, so the main value Athena claims is described but not demonstrated.
findings.source: "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: The transition cards are dense, with exit codes, guards, locks and records. A newcomer who does not use firstmate will struggle with them. The 'Start here' section is the part they can actually use.
findings.source: Transitions section, e.g. t2 "Every worker place is held, so the spawn is deferred with exit 75 ... lock contention or an unreadable capacity declaration refuses with exit 1"

findings.text: Each state line shows only a name and a tag such as "waiting", with no description. The reader must go to the Glossary to find out what "close-pending" or "ready" means.
findings.source: States of a piece of work: "Read each line as the state's name, its kind, and the claims that support it."

findings.text: The page contradicts itself on red PRs. Several places say "never" (yolo entry, t10, "What firstmate is"), while the 'red' entry and claim c28 allow a waiver from the captain.
findings.source: Glossary 'yolo': "it never merges a red PR" vs 'red': "unless a current explicit captain instruction names the check to waive"

findings.text: This link in the header assumes the reader is an owner with pending proposals. To a newcomer it is unexplained and distracting.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: This section uses internal repository details that mean nothing to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"

findings.text: The 'Words used first' list uses "green" and "in scope" in the yolo definition before defining them. "In scope" is then admitted to have no test, which leaves a key term vague.
findings.source: Words used first: "yolo ... firstmate merges green work that is in scope itself" defined before "green" and "in scope"
